answer: Delayed beacon admission lottery. Identities lock public keys; a verifiable random beacon, the river of seed material, publishes only after lock. Each key must solve a puzzle seeded by that beacon and its key, target 2^20 hash evaluations, and only solved keys may act that epoch. Since the seed is unknown beforehand, an attacker cannot precompute or reuse work. Every sybil key needs fresh computation after the beacon, costing about one CPU-hour apiece. A walnut-sized precomputed farm gives no advantage. No pearl of reusable work remains across identities.
